newsitem.title: USA: Gasoline aids outright cash crudes in U.S. Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Gasoline aids outright cash crudes in U.S. Gulf.

text.p: Cash crude grade differentials in the U.S. Gulf failed to budge Friday afternoon, but outright prices recovered off a NYMEX uptick about $20.00 a barrel.
At 1312 EDT (1712 GMT), September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood 5-10 cents higher at $20.15-25 a barrel, and September/October spreads were -5/3 cents.

Cash crude traders remarked on the lack of players in the market, leaving only a nominal level of reported deals. Midland/WTI was sold in the early-going at 28 cents under September WTI/Cushing, steady from markings seen for most of the last week.

Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James ranged at a 23-25 cents premium to the same September marker, failing to sell, traders said. Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire did attract a deal at the unchanged level of 20 cents under WTI.
September WTI/Cushing Postings Plus was done at $1.98.

Reports from Venezuela said PDVSA's 310,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery in Curacao was expected to reach crude throughput of 120,000 bpd within one to two weeks. The plant was disabled by a serious fire on Thursday morning, which cut throughput by 130,000 bpd to 60,000 bpd.
Outright crude also gained on the rally in unleaded gasoline futures, where NYMEX prices surged past 64.00 cents a gallon for September.
